text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, which helps both you and your teammates work faster. One key habit is following naming conventions: choose clear, descriptive names for variables so their purpose is obvious. Another important idea is keeping functions small and focused, so each one does a single job well. This makes the code simpler to test and reuse. Finally, clean code is easier to maintain, because future changes cause fewer bugs and take less time. In short, writing clean code saves effort and leads to better software.
